blocks.text: This article provides a summary of all new features and enhancements per Zscaler cloud for Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA). Zscaler will email a notification to your organization's registered support contacts approximately one week before your cloud is upgraded. To see scheduled maintenance updates for your cloud, visit the Trust Portal.

blocks.heading: Deprecation of SSPM Policies for Microsoft 365

blocks.text: The following policies are deprecated for Microsoft 365 in both SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) Essentials and Advanced SSPM:

blocks.item: Set Automated Notifications for New and Trending Cloud Applications in Our Organization
Set Automated Notification for New OAuth Applications Connected to Your Corporate Environment

blocks.text: To learn more, see Viewing and Managing the Supported SSPM Policies and What Is Advanced Posture Management?

blocks.heading: Enhanced Logging of Collaborator Group Members

blocks.text: This enhancement allows you to view logs for individual members within a collaborator group. As part of the update, the following changes are available in the ZIA Admin Portal:

blocks.heading: SaaS Security Insights Logs and SaaS Security Assets with Incidents

blocks.text: When an individual file is shared with a group, you can view logs for individual members of a group who are either internal collaborators or external collaborators, depending upon the type of domain they belong to in the SaaS Security Insights Logs page and the Assets Report: Assets with Incidents page (Analytics > SaaS Security > Assets > click an application or tenant).
To learn more, see About SaaS Security Insights Logs and Understanding the Assets Report: Assets with Incidents.

blocks.heading: SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning DLP Actions

blocks.text: For file sharing applications, the DLP actions Remove Internal Collaborators, Remove External Collaborators, and Remove External Collaborators and Shareable Link also remove internal and external collaborator groups along with all individual internal and external collaborators. To remove an individual collaborator from an external group, you can use the Remove External Collaborators action on the Remediation page to manually remove the collaborator.
To learn more, see Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy with Content Inspection and Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy without Content Inspection.

blocks.heading: Enhancement to URL Filtering Policy Page

blocks.text: On the URL Filtering Policy page (Policy > URL & Cloud App Control > URL Filtering Policy), the URL Filtering rules are paginated with up to 100 rules displayed per page.
See image.
You can filter and search for URL Filtering rules based on the following categories:
See image.
To learn more, see About URL Filtering.

blocks.heading: Updates to the Rule Labels and URL Filtering Policy endpoint categories

blocks.text: You can retrieve a list of rule labels based on the specified rule type using the GET /ruleLabels/ruleType/{ruleType} endpoint and retrieve the count of URL Filtering rules using the GET urlFilteringRules/count endpoint.

Two new query parameters, page and pageSize are available for the GET /urlFilteringRules endpoint. When you do not specify the page and pageSize query parameters, the default values are used. To learn more, see Fetching URL Filtering Rules Using Pagination and Search Filters.
To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.
The following platforms support 64 GB of RAM and 3 antivirus (AV) engines per Virtual Service Edge:
This allows you to scan large files and maintain Virtual Service Edge performance. You can deploy Virtual Service Edge either in standalone or cluster mode.
Generative AI (Gen AI) prompts that are displayed in the Web Insights Logs can be obfuscated when adding admin roles.
See image.
To learn more, see About the Gen AI Security Report.

blocks.heading: Granular Control for Atlassian AI Application

blocks.text: You can allow or block the use of embedded AI applications on Atlassian sites and enable or disable Zscaler to store the generative AI prompts entered in these embedded AI applications per cloud app control rule. As part of this feature, the following fields appear in the Add/Edit Productivity and CRM Tools Rule window only for the Atlassian application:
See image.
To learn more, see Adding a Productivity & CRM Tools Rule for Cloud App Control.
An Application Activity, Embedded AI, is added to the Web Insights Logs for Atlassian applications only.
See image.
To learn more, see Web Insights Logs: Filters.

blocks.heading: Logs for Email Received and Sent Time

blocks.text: The following enhancements are available for Insights and NSS Feeds in the ZIA Admin Portal to record the time Zscaler either received or sent an email response.

New columns Zscaler Sent Time and Zscaler Received Time are added to Email DLP Insights Logs. The Scan Time field is enhanced to reflect the duration of time (milliseconds) from when Zscaler receives an email until the Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy evaluation is complete.
See image.
To learn more, see Email DLP Insights Logs: Columns.

The fields %s{zs_rcv_time} and %s{zs_sent_time} can be added to the Feed Output Format when configuring NSS or Cloud NSS feeds for Email DLP logs. The %llu{scan_time} field is enhanced to reflect the duration of time (milliseconds) from when Zscaler receives an email until the DLP policy evaluation is complete.
To learn more, see NSS Feed Output Format: Email DLP Logs.

blocks.heading: Pattern Requirements for Custom DLP Dictionaries

blocks.text: For custom Data Loss Prevention (DLP) dictionaries that use patterns with lookaround constructs (also known as zero-length assertions), the Zscaler service now enforces the following restrictions:

blocks.item: You must select Match Any Patterns and Any Phrases as the Match Type.
You must configure at least one phrase.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Adding Custom DLP Dictionaries.

When scheduling a scan for SaaS applications tenants (Policy > SaaS Security > Scan Configuration > Add Scan Schedule), you can also configure the polling interval based on how often you want the system to scan the application.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring SaaS Security Scan Schedules.

blocks.heading: Support for Number of Collaborators for File Sharing Apps in DLP

blocks.text: The SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy supports the number of internal and external collaborators as scoping criteria for all file sharing applications, including Box, Dropbox, Confluence, ShareFile, and Smartsheet. Administrators can monitor file sharing among collaborators by applying the scope to a number of internal and external collaborators.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the Data At Rest Scanning DLP Policy and About Data at Rest Scanning DLP.

blocks.heading: Support for Quarantine File to Desired Location for File Sharing Apps

blocks.text: The support for quarantining files in a desired location has been extended to all file sharing apps, including Box, Dropbox, Confluence, ShareFile, and Smartsheet. This feature was already available for Google Drive, OneDrive, and SharePoint apps. You can specify a quarantine location for files violating DLP policy rules at the time of onboarding the tenant.
On the Edit DLP Rule window, a new action called Admin Quarantine is available for all tenants with a defined quarantine location.
See image.

To learn more, see About Data at Rest Scanning DLP, Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy with Content Inspection, and Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy without Content Inspection.

blocks.heading: Automatic Local Language Translation for Isolation in ZIA

blocks.text: Automatic language translation is globally available for Isolation. The isolated session localizes the language based on the user's browser language settings, and displays that language on the rendered web page.
To learn more, see Understanding Language Translate for Isolation.

blocks.heading: Original URL for Isolation Profiles in ZIA

blocks.text: Original URL has replaced Local Browser Rendering in Isolation. It is now an option that admins can configure in isolation profiles. This means that the user of the isolation profile sees the native browser URL of the web page that loads when entering Isolation.
To learn more, see User Experience Modes in Isolation and Original URL for Isolation.

blocks.heading: Visual Indicator for Turbo Mode in Isolation for ZIA

blocks.text: If Turbo Mode is enabled on an isolation profile and the user also has hardware acceleration enabled, the appearance of the zGPU icon next to the Turbo Mode command is displayed in the Isolation Bar.
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding Turbo Mode for Isolation.

blocks.heading: Updates to Firewall Dashboard and Insights

blocks.text: On the Firewall Insights page (Analytics > Firewall Insights), the maximum number of rules displayed for the Rule Name data type has been increased. When using bar or table charts, you can view up to the top 4,000 rules (in increments of 500, 1,000, 2,000, and 4,000) by selecting the value from the drop-down menu.
In addition, the charts explicitly show rules that were not triggered during the selected time frame, displaying them with a zero hit count if they fall within the specified rule limit.
See image.

The Firewall Overview dashboard includes additional time filters, allowing you to view data over 48-hour, 3-day, 5-day, and 7-day intervals. Additionally, widgets using the Rule Name data type display hit counts for all rules when viewed as bar and table charts.
In addition, the charts explicitly show rules that were not triggered during the selected time frame, displaying them with a zero hit count if they fall within the specified rule limit.
See image.

These time and value filter enhancements allow you to track rule hit counts over extended time periods, helping you analyze rule utilization and optimize or refine your firewall rule configurations based on real-world traffic patterns.

blocks.heading: Create VM Instance using the Virtual Service Edge Amazon Web Services Terraform Modules

blocks.text: You can create a virtual machine (VM) in Amazon Web Services (AWS) using the Virtual Service Edge Terraform modules.
To learn more, see Configuring Virtual Service Edge for Amazon Web Services and Configuring Virtual Service Edge for Amazon Web Services with GWLB.

blocks.heading: Gen AI Prompt Configuration for Claude and Mistral

blocks.text: Zscaler's Gen AI prompt configuration is extended to the Claude and Mistral generative AI applications. You can enable prompts for these generative AI applications to categorize and store the prompts for the respective applications.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Advanced Policy Settings.

blocks.heading: Added Claude and Mistral Capabilities to URL & Cloud App Control Policy Settings Endpoint

blocks.text: Two new Boolean fields, enableClaudePrompt and enableMistralAIPrompt, are available for the AdvancedUrlFilteringCloudAppOptions model in the /advancedUrlFilterAndCloudAppSettings APIs. These fields allow users to use generative AI prompts with Claude and Mistral.
To learn more, see URL & Cloud App Control Policy Settings.

blocks.heading: Enhancement to Filters in 3rd-Party App Governance and Advanced SSPM

blocks.text: In the App Inventory and User Inventory, and on the Posture page, the filter options that don't currently exist in your organization display separately and do not return results. You can still select them when creating new views and policies. If a new app in your organization matches a policy, the policy is triggered and the filter options will be included in your organization.
See image.
To learn more, see App Inventory Filters, About User Inventory, and About Posture.

blocks.heading: Support for GitHub User Email Enrichment in 3rd-Party App Governance

blocks.text: The Users page displays multiple emails in addition to public emails for GitHub users. These emails are associated with the domain of the organization that owns the GitHub account. This enhancement improves the ability to find user and admin emails from outside the domain.
To learn more, see About User Inventory.
The 3rd-Party App Governance API adds a new endpoint, /app_views/{appViewId}/accounts, to retrieve users' email addresses associated with specific app IDs.
/app_views/{appViewId}/apps_extended provides the total number of enabled users totalenabledusers within its response.
To learn more about this endpoint, see the Understanding ZIA APIs and API Rate Limit Summary.

blocks.heading: Support for Google Workspace OU Segregation

blocks.text: You can segregate your Google Workspace integration by organizational units (OUs) in 3rd-Party App Governance. This segregation ensures that each OU can access only its relevant users, applications, and posture data, while maintaining consolidated tenant management for admins.
To enable this feature, contact Zscaler Support.
To learn more, see Integrating with Google Workspace.

blocks.heading: Enhancements to Endpoint DLP for Windows

blocks.text: The following enhancements are available in Zscaler Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) for Windows:

blocks.heading: Endpoint DLP Support for Clipboard and Application File Access

blocks.text: To access this feature, contact your Zscaler Account team.
Endpoint DLP supports monitoring and blocking sensitive information when specific applications access files, as well as when content is pasted into those applications.
To get started, configure the relevant applications to prevent sensitive data loss on the DLP Resources page (Administration > DLP Resources):
See Image.
Once applications are defined, you can create Endpoint DLP policy rules that:

blocks.item: Protect file access: Use Application File Access as the channel to detect and block sensitive data exposed when applications read files.
Protect clipboard activity: Use Clipboard as the channel to detect and block sensitive data pasted into applications.

blocks.text: See Image.
To learn more, see About DLP Resources, Adding DLP Resources and Configuring Endpoint DLP Policy Rules.

blocks.heading: Removable Storage Rule: Device Per User Pair

blocks.text: Streamline management of the Device Control Removable Storage rules by defining multiple removable storage devices and mapping them to specific users or endpoints within a single rule. This rule also supports CSV file import for bulk operations.
See Image.
To learn more, see Managing a Removable Storage Rule.

blocks.heading: Endpoint Data Scan - End User Report

blocks.text: This feature introduces configurable reports to increase transparency for end users. These reports aim at providing users with best practices and show them where sensitive data is stored locally on their endpoints. This feature aims at making endpoint data scanning more efficient, transparent, and collaborative, improving how administrators and end users work together to manage sensitive data.
To learn more, see Understanding End User Reports, About Endpoint Data Scan, and Analyzing Endpoint DLP Scan for a User.
This release introduces the following expanded configuration options across Endpoint Data Scan, Classification, and DLP inspection to improve performance, control, and flexibility:

blocks.item: Granular controls for End User report visibility, scheduling, sensitive data exposure, and custom messages.
Ability to exclude specific file systems, folders, and entities.
Option to skip files created by high-volume applications (e.g., compilers) during continuous classification, while still enforcing real-time inspection for exfiltration events.
Ability to disable OCR for Continuous Classification and Print Control.
Configurable maximum file size and timeout strategies with Allow or Block fallback actions.
Per-channel application exclusions for Printer, Clipboard, Removable Storage, and Network Share inspection.
Option to disable Microsoft Office printing add-ins (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), limiting inspection to print spooler content when disabled.
Improved removable storage accuracy by ignoring vendor-specific local drives misidentified as removable devices.
Option to hide the Protect action for end users.

blocks.text: See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Endpoint Data Scan and Endpoint Settings and Activating Device Control Policy Rules and Configuration Changes.

The Zscaler Applications page (Analytics > Endpoint Data Scan > Inventory > Applications) provides insights into executable files and applications stored on endpoints, gathering data on installed software, running processes, and libraries. This is crucial not only for compliance, but also for monitoring, auditing, and identifying vulnerabilities or unauthorized software.
See image.
To learn more, see About Inventory and Analyzing Application Details.

The Zscaler Device Investigation page (Analytics > Endpoint Data Scan > Device Investigation) provides a comprehensive view of all the endpoint details, including real-time device health status. You can view all the detected applications and the sensitive files stored on the endpoint.
See image.
To learn more, see About Device Investigation and Analyzing Device Investigation Details.
To access this feature, contact your Zscaler Account team.

This new capability allows for the detection of data exfiltration on Endpoint DLP channels by matching full or partial content against indexed documents. A secure, endpoint-based workflow has been introduced in this release, enabling authorized users to index sensitive documents directly from their endpoints using the Endpoint DLP context menu. The Endpoint IDM operates in parallel to the Inline DLP IDM. Enforcement and detection are independent and require reindexing of IDM files using the Endpoint DLP. This feature is currently in limited availability. You can access the Sensitive Information page from Analytics > Endpoint Data Scan > Sensitive Information.
See image.
To learn more, see About Sensitive Information and Configuring Sensitive Information Settings.

blocks.heading: Additional Support for Predefined DLP Dictionaries in Endpoint DLP

blocks.text: The following predefined Data Loss Prevention (DLP) dictionaries are supported for use in Endpoint DLP policy rules:
To learn more, see Understanding Predefined DLP Dictionaries.

blocks.heading: Added Context for Endpoint DLP Triggers

blocks.text: You can see an additional 15-byte prefix and suffix to the left and right of the Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) trigger that provides more information about the Endpoint DLP incident. The additional context can be seen in the Incident Receiver, Zscaler Workflow Automation, and Email Notifications.
The following image shows an example of trigger context in Zscaler Workflow Automation:

To learn more, see Configuring DLP Notification Templates, Configuring the Zscaler Incident Receiver for On-Premises VMs, Configuring the Zscaler Incident Receiver for Amazon Web Services EC2 VMs, and Configuring the Zscaler Incident Receiver for Azure VMs.

blocks.heading: Endpoint DLP Support for Proximity Length in Predefined Dictionaries

blocks.text: The Zscaler service supports the Proximity Length field on applicable predefined Data Loss Prevention (DLP) dictionaries when used in engines associated with Endpoint DLP rules. The proximity length defines how close a high confidence phrase must be to an instance of the pattern (that the dictionary detects) to count as a match. For certain predefined DLP dictionaries, the Proximity Length field appears when the dictionary’s Confidence Score Threshold is High.
See Image.
To learn more, see Understanding Predefined DLP Dictionaries.

blocks.heading: Support for New SSPM Controls for GitHub

blocks.text: The number of SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) controls for GitHub in Advanced SSPM has been increased. Eleven new SSPM controls are supported for GitHub.
The Zscaler service can capture traffic in multiple ways:

blocks.item: Traffic Capture Essentials: Capture traffic as PCAP files with supported actions in ZIA policies when traffic matches policy criteria.
Traffic Capture for Network Detection and Response (NDR): Capture traffic as PCAPNG files based on criteria specified by the Traffic Capture policy.

blocks.text: Traffic Capture for NDR introduces a standalone Traffic Capture policy page (Policy > Traffic Capture) that enables granular control of Traffic Capture triggers, sampling, and how much traffic is collected per captured connection.
See image.
Information in Traffic Capture for NDR data can be obfuscated on the Traffic Capture Settings page (Administration > Traffic Capture).
See image.
To access Traffic Capture Essentials and Traffic Capture for NDR, contact your Zscaler Account team.

All Zscaler Traffic Capture methods are enabled and disabled on the Traffic Capture Settings page (Administration > Traffic Capture). Connection to your organization's Amazon S3 bucket is also configured on the Traffic Capture Settings page. To learn more, see About Traffic Capture Settings.
To learn more about the Traffic Capture policy, see About Traffic Capture Policy.

The cloud service API includes the following new endpoints to create, update, and delete Traffic Capture policy rules as well as retrieve information for all or specific rules. In addition, they allow you to retrieve the rule count, rule order information, and rule label associations.
To learn more, see the API Reference.

blocks.heading: Web EUN for DNS Control Policy

blocks.text: The DNS Control policy includes an option to display a notification to end users when the policy blocks access to specific domains. Zscaler hosts this End User Notification (EUN) page, eliminating the need for organizations to host their own EUN web page. The DNS EUN web page informs users of the reason for blocking access to specific domains per your organization's security policy. You can customize the notification to display your organization's name, logo, and a custom message.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the DNS Control Policy, DNS End User Notifications, and Understanding Browser-Based End User Notifications.

blocks.heading: Apply MIP Label as Manual Remediation Action in SaaS Security Assets

blocks.text: For file sharing applications OneDrive and SharePoint, you can apply the MIP label as a manual remediation action from the SaaS Security Assets with Incidents page (Analytics > SaaS Security > Assets > click an application or tenant).
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding the Assets Report: Assets with Incidents and Understanding SaaS Security API Supported Capabilities.

blocks.heading: Additional Logging of Users Performing Actions on File

blocks.text: You can identify and report not only the owner of the file, but also the user who last modified or shared a file that caused a DLP violation, in the ZIA Admin Portal. As part of this feature, the following enhancements are available for Insights Logs and NSS Feeds:
The following filters and columns are available on the SaaS Security Insights and SaaS Assets With Incidents page:

blocks.item: Filters: Last Modified User and Last Shared User
Columns: Last Modified User, Last Shared User, and Last Shared On

blocks.text: See image.
To learn more, see About the SaaS Security Insights Logs Page and Understanding the Assets Report: Assets with Incidents.

You can add the following fields to the SaaS Security logs Feed Output Format when configuring NSS or Cloud NSS feeds for file applications. These fields provide information on the user who last modified the file, shared the file, and the timestamp when the file was shared, which triggered DLP violations:
To learn more, see NSS Feed Output Format: SaaS Security Logs.

blocks.heading: Create VM Instance using the Virtual Service Edge Azure Terraform Modules

blocks.text: You can create a virtual machine (VM) in Azure using the Virtual Service Edge Terraform modules.
To learn more, see Configuring Virtual Service Edge for Microsoft Azure.

blocks.heading: Enhancement to Custom Views in 3rd-Party App Governance

blocks.text: When creating and saving a custom view in 3rd-Party App Governance, you can update the saved view to include your current tenant selection on the global platform filters.
See image.
To learn more, see Custom Views.

Zscaler supports Creative Commons (CC) search for certain search engines (i.e., Bing, Google, and Yahoo). This allows you to see only search results that are licensed under CC. The Enable Creative Commons Search Results option is added to the Policy > URL & Cloud App Control > Advanced Policy Settings page as part of this feature.
This option is disabled by default.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Advanced Policy Settings.

blocks.heading: Zscaler Client Connector EUNs for Firewall, DNS, and IPS Policies

blocks.text: Beginning with Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 for Windows, ZIA Firewall policies—including Firewall Filtering, DNS Control, and IPS Control—support end user notifications (EUNs) via Zscaler Client Connector. When configuring these policy rules, you can select to show a notification to users and select the notification message that must appear when the rule is triggered. This feature is available on Windows devices running Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 or later over Z-Tunnel 2.0.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the Firewall Filtering Policy, Configuring the DNS Control Policy, and Configuring the IPS Control Policy.

You can customize the EUNs for these policy rules under Administration > End User Notifications > Client Connector. You can modify the default notification message and additionally create custom messages to allow the selection of different notification messages for individual policy rules.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring EUNs for Firewall Filtering, Configuring EUNs for DNS Control, Configuring EUNs for IPS Control.

You can define scope types and values to map the workload traffic to a sublocation. Defining scopes allows you to apply granular ZIA and Cloud Connector security policies to the workload traffic from that sublocation. You can configure scopes only for Workload traffic type sublocations whose parent locations are associated with Amazon Web Services (AWS) Cloud Connector groups.
As part of this feature, the following fields are added to the Administration > Location Management > Locations > Add Sublocation window:
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing Sublocations, Configuring Sublocations, and Using Sublocation Scopes to Group Cloud Connector Workloads
The Location and LocationLite models used in /locations endpoints within the cloud service API include the following new attributes to support these functionalities via API:
To learn more, see the API Reference.
JSON Web Token (JWT) authentication is available for Zscaler Cloud & Branch Connector workloads. JWT authentication is enabled when configuring locations.
See image.
JWT authentication is not supported for the Extranet and IoT Traffic location types.
You can configure JWT authentication exemptions on the Advanced Settings page.
See image.
Token validators for JWT authentication are configured in the Authentication Service Admin Portal.
To learn more, see Understanding JWT Authentication.

blocks.heading: JWT Authentication Support for Workloads on Management Portal for Partners

blocks.text: The ZIA Admin Portal supports a new method, JWT authentication, to authenticate workloads from Cloud & Branch Connector.

In the Management Portal for Partners, you can enable this feature in ZIA for your tenants by using the JWT Auth for Workload field on the Tenant Details page (Tenant > Tenant Details page > Special Settings). To enable this for your tenants, contact the Zscaler Support team.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing Tenant Details.

blocks.heading: Support for Enhanced US Driver's License Dictionary and Sub-Dictionaries

blocks.text: The Zscaler service supports the Enhanced Driver's License (United States) predefined Data Loss Prevention (DLP) dictionary. The parent dictionary contains predefined sub-dictionaries for all 50 U.S. states, plus the District of Columbia, and each sub-dictionary can be individually referenced in your DLP engines.
On the DLP Dictionaries & Engines page (Administration > DLP Dictionaries & Engines), you can expand the Enhanced Driver's License (United States) to see each of the state sub-dictionaries.
See image.
You can then configure each of the individual state sub-dictionaries to set the Confidence Score Threshold, Proximity Length, and any Custom High Confidence Phrases.
See image.

blocks.item: The Enhanced Driver's License (United States) dictionary is not supported for Endpoint DLP.
The legacy Driver's License (United States) dictionary has been replaced, but not deprecated, by the Enhanced Driver's License (United States) predefined dictionary.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Understanding Predefined DLP Dictionaries.
You can retrieve the SaaS Security Scan Configuration information and the validation status of a SaaS application tenant using the following endpoints:
To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.
The Postman collection is also updated to include new and updated resources.
To learn more, see Configuring the Postman REST API Client.

Isolated sessions now automatically restore their web pages if they time out on a user's device. If a session is idle for longer than the timeout of 10 minutes, the isolated page automatically refreshes itself, and the user does not have to sign in again. When this action occurs, the banner notification announcing the start of isolation is disabled. This feature is different than Persistent State, which is enabled per isolation profile to carry over data from an expired session to a new session.
To learn more, see Using Persistent State for Isolation.

blocks.heading: Original URL of Website Name in Isolation

blocks.text: The UI is updated so that when users enter an isolated session, they now see the original URL of the website they are on instead of the isolation web page URL. This change provides users with an experience with a look and feel more like a native browser compared to the container view of being isolated.
To learn more, see User Experience Modes in Isolation.
New cloud applications are added to the cloud application categories. You can download the list of newly added cloud applications to the respective categories: Download
The risk index and risk attribute values for these new applications are visible only after they are available on all the clouds.
AI or machine language classification is extended to support around 200 new document types across 10 common document categories.

As part of this extended support, Insights Logs and the Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) are enhanced to provide enriched auto-classification of documents that are uploaded or downloaded during transactions.
The following enhancements are available in the ZIA Admin Portal:

A new filter and column, Subdocument Type, is added to the Web Insights Logs and SaaS Security Insights Logs pages to capture, categorize, and log document subtypes related to administrative documents, invoices, expense reports, and more.
See image.
To learn more, see Web Insights Logs: Filters, Web Insights Logs: Columns, and About SaaS Security Insights Logs.

The field %s{upload_doc_sub_type} can be added to the Feed Output Format when configuring an NSS or Cloud NSS feed for web logs. Additionally, the field %s{upload_doc_subtype} is available for SaaS Security feeds configured for file applications (e.g., Box). Both fields log the subtype (e.g., Financial Statements: Income Statements (Profit and Loss Statements)) of uploaded or downloaded documents.
To learn more, see NSS Feed Output Format: Web Logs​​​​​​ and NSS Feed Output Format: SaaS Security Logs.

SafeSearch allows granular control of applications. This allows you to apply SafeSearch to specific applications. As part of this change, on the Advanced Policy Settings page (Policies > URL & Cloud App Control > Advanced Policy Settings), the SafeSearch Applications drop-down appears when you enable the Enforce SafeSearch option, which lists applications.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Advanced Policy Settings.

blocks.heading: Enhancement to the URL & Cloud App Control Policy Settings Endpoint

blocks.text: A new field safeSearchApps is available for the AdvancedUrlFilteringCloudAppOptions model, referenced in the /advancedUrlFilterAndCloudAppSettings endpoint.
To learn more, go to AdvancedUrlFilteringCloudAppOptions from URL & Cloud App Control Policy Settings.

blocks.text: The File Type Control and Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies support the following file types in the Other category:
The file types are available when creating the following policies:
To learn more, see About File Type Control and About Data Loss Prevention.

blocks.heading: New Network Applications in Firewall Control

blocks.text: Zscaler includes support for identifying several new network applications using deep packet inspection and controlling the network application traffic using Firewall Filtering rules. These network applications are listed on the Network Applications page (Administration > Network Applications) and are available to be configured in Firewall Filtering rules (Policy > Firewall Control > Firewall Filtering Policy).
List of New Network Applications
To learn more, see About Network Applications and Configuring the Firewall Filtering Policy.
You can view information about the number of transactions per application based on their status (blocked or allowed) in the Cloud Applications table of the Shadow IT Report.
A new column, No. of Transactions, is added to the Cloud Applications table.
See image.
To learn more, see About the Shadow IT Report.

blocks.heading: Support for Custom File Types in DLP and File Type Control Policies

blocks.text: You can create custom file types and use them when creating Data Loss Prevention (DLP) and File Type Control policies. You can then filter and view logs for these custom file types in Web Insights Logs and the Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS).
See image.
As part of this enhancement, the Download User-Defined File Type and Upload User-Defined File Type filters and columns are added to the Web Insights Logs.
See Image.
To learn more, see:

blocks.item: Configuring the File Type Control Policy
Configuring DLP Policy Rules with Evaluate All Rules Mode Enabled
Configuring DLP Policy Rules with Content Inspection
Configuring DLP Policy Rules without Content Inspection

blocks.text: Additionally, filters for Download User-Defined File Type and Upload User-Defined File Type are added to NSS and Cloud NSS feeds for web logs as well as Microsoft Cloud App Security (MCAS) NSS feeds. You can use these filters to limit the logs sent to your security information and event management (SIEM) system based on the custom type of files that were downloaded or uploaded during the transaction.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding NSS Feeds for Web Logs, Adding Cloud NSS Feeds for Web Logs, and Adding MCAS NSS Feeds.

The cloud service API includes the following new endpoints to create, update, and delete custom file types, retrieve information about custom file types and the count of custom file types, and retrieve information about all file types that can be used as rule conditions in DLP and File Type Control policies.

blocks.text: The Zscaler Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Exact Data Match (EDM) dictionary search score total matchCount has been enhanced to be based on the number of unique sets of matches found in the content.

Previously, matchCount was determined by the number of matches across all rows and all templates specified in active dictionaries, and only unique templates contributed to the matchCount total. If multiple dictionaries used the same template, each instance of the template was counted as a separate match. With this update, matchCount is based on unique token matches, irrespective of the templates or dictionaries used, and only unorder unique sets of matches are counted. Additionally, the distinction between primary and secondary fields is no longer applicable; all matches are counted equally.

blocks.heading: SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning DLP Support for Trusted Users and Trusted Domains

The Zscaler service treats trusted domains and trusted users the same as internal domains and internal users.
See image.
Trusted users and trusted domains are configured as recipient profiles and domain profiles, respectively, in the Email Profiles for your organization.

When evaluating rules, if a file matches all rule criteria and the trusted users or trusted domains set for the rule, the Zscaler service does not consider a transaction to be a rule violation and does not take action on the file.
To learn more, see Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy with Content Inspection, Configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP Policy without Content Inspection, and About Email Profiles.

blocks.heading: Support for Zscaler-Managed Business Continuity Cloud

blocks.heading: Support for Dedicated IP and Geolocalization IP

blocks.text: The Dedicated IP feature allows organizations to subscribe to dedicated IP addresses for the Zscaler data centers of their choice. Users can use these dedicated IP addresses (unique to the organization) as their source IP address to reach destinations that require source IP-based access.

The Geolocalization IP feature allows organizations located across countries to forward traffic via source IP addresses mapped to the country from where the traffic originates. This enables users to access destinations (e.g., government websites) that require the country's local source IP address for access.
The dedicated IP and the geolocalization IP features leverage ZIA forwarding policies to forward traffic.
As part of this feature, the following enhancements are available in the ZIA Admin Portal:

To learn more, see About Dedicated IP Addresses.

blocks.text: Two new forwarding methods, Dedicated IP and Geo IP, are added when configuring traffic forwarding rules.

blocks.item: Use the Dedicated IP forwarding method to forward traffic to destinations using the source IP addresses provisioned for the organization.
Use the Geo IP forwarding method to forward traffic to destinations using the source IP address mapped to the country from where the traffic originates.

Zscaler Extranet Application Support provides organizations with a secure way to access resources from partners that are not using the Zscaler service. This is typically accomplished with site-to-site VPN tunnels which present organizational, financial, and security drawbacks. Zscaler Extranet Application Support provides access to partner resources through IPSec tunnels, retaining the benefits of the Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) without requiring partners to install hardware and software.
Extranet resources are created on the Extranet page. Each resource is configured with one or more traffic selectors and DNS servers.
See image.
Extranet resources must be assigned to locations in order to grant users access to the partner resource. Extranet is available as a Location Type when configuring locations.
See image.
Selecting Extranet as the Location type prompts the user to select an Extranet Resource, Traffic Selector, and DNS Server.
See image.

After extranet locations are configured in the ZIA Admin Portal, they become available in the ZPA Admin Portal when configuring server groups and application segments. You can configure ZPA access policies to manage extranet applications.

To learn more about Extranet Application Support, see Understanding Extranet Application Support, About Extranet, and Configuring an Extranet. Ranges and limitations for Extranet Application Support are listed on Ranges & Limitations.

To learn more, see Adding NSS Feeds for Tunnel Logs and Adding Cloud NSS Feeds for Tunnel Logs.
